principles.text: Hooks are designed to create a curiosity loop, like a rabbit hole in the viewer's brain, making them unable to stop watching.
Create curiosity by introducing a contrasting alternative to the viewer's initial belief (A vs. B).
Hooks must make an impact and stick within the first five seconds.
The Fortuneteller hook leverages the brain's natural tendency to think about the future.
The Magician hook acts as a 'stun gun' using outlandish, rhythmic, or visually popping elements to stop the scroll and force attention.
A passive visual activity in the background (visual pacifier) occupies subconscious attention, allowing the viewer to focus on the main content without churning.

The best way to create curiosity is with contrast. The hook introduces an alternative (B) to what the viewer currently believes (A), and the distance between A and B is the contrast. Bigger contrast leads to more curiosity.
You only have approximately 5 seconds to make the hook stick and grab the viewer's attention.
Use outlandish, rhythmic, or visually popping elements to stop the scroll and capture immediate attention.
The best way to create a curiosity loop is with contrast; the bigger the contrast, the more curiosity and deeper the hook.
The human brain is designed to constantly think about the future, which can be leveraged for hooks.
Strategically use visuals and/or language to visually force the viewer's attention to a specific thing.
Strategic visuals can force viewer attention to a specific thing.

formulas.name: Fortuneteller
formulas.template: Present vs. Future: Establish current reality, hint at future change, tease new future as possibility.

formulas.name: Experimenter
formulas.template: Peer-to-Peer Demo: Establish pain point, show how a new method/tool solved it via experiment, explain why it works.
examples: Does anything look weird about this shot?
ChatGPT's new AI agent controls my computer!

formulas.name: Teacher
formulas.template: Teacher-to-Student Lesson: Establish pain point, present a solution/learning, explain how it works to help them win.
examples: 3 things you can learn from Aritzia.
Here's how I got this shot.

formulas.name: Magician
formulas.template: Stun Gun: Use a quick, atypical, visually/audibly stunning element to grab attention, then transition to another hook format.

formulas.name: Investigator
formulas.template: Secret/Unknown: Tee up a secret or unknown finding, then reveal it, creating contrast between not knowing and knowing.
examples: Secret Japanese city at Mount Fuji.

formulas.name: Contrarian
formulas.template: Direct Challenge: State a belief that directly contradicts conventional wisdom or common practice.
examples: Why don't more brands do this?
Your space sucks, no creative ideas.

twitch_comp_notes: For mute-first burned captions on Twitch reaction clips, leverage visual 'stun gun' tactics (Magician hook) and rhythmic elements to grab attention quickly.
Utilize 'visual pacifiers' (passive background activity) to maintain subconscious engagement while the main text hook is processed.

Leverage visual elements (as in the 'Magician' hook concept) to 'stun' and stop the scroll, even if the burned text is the primary hook.
Direct 'Contrarian' statements (a 'contrarian snapback') work exceptionally well for immediate attention in a mute-first environment.
'Fortune Teller' hooks should concisely hint at future changes or impacts to spark curiosity, as the text is the primary information carrier.
